affectedPublicSurfaces: THE PRODUCTION PROMPT VERSION PIN — the one genuinely seller-visible effect in this slice. `prompts/composer.py` holds `PRODUCTION_PROMPT_VERSION: dict[str, int] = {OPTIMIZE_PRODUCT_PLAYBOOK.workflow_key: 3}`, so every run created today is pinned to v3 by `approval.py::_resolve_prompt_pin` → `prompts.production_version(workflow_key)` → `prompt_version(...)`/`prompt_sha256(...)`, stamped onto `workflow_runs.prompt_version`/`prompt_sha256`. Extracting shared sections CHANGES the composed bytes, so a new version file `prompts/optimize_product/v4.md` is added and the pin moves 3 → 4. From the deploy forward, every new run executes different prompt bytes; that is a change to what the model is told, and it reaches a real seller on the first run after cutover.

The prompt COMPOSITION structure: `prompts/` holds only `composer.py` and `optimize_product/{v1,v2,v3}.md` today, and `_WORKFLOW_BINDINGS` (a `dict[str, _WorkflowPromptBinding]`) has exactly ONE entry, keyed on `OPTIMIZE_PRODUCT_PLAYBOOK.workflow_key`. This slice moves the workflow-invariant sections (role, mandate, source-role rules, prohibitions) into shared section files composed into every workflow prompt, and makes the binding a registry entry per workflow supplied by #1702's playbook registry.

THE THREE PINNED GATE TESTS, and the count matters: `PLAN.md` says two, the code has THREE, all importing `WORKFLOW_KEY` from `playbooks/optimize_product.py` — `tests/unit/test_agent_prompt_snapshot_gate.py` (byte-for-byte against `tests/fixtures/agent_prompt_gates/optimize_product_v{1,2,3}_composed.golden.md`), `tests/unit/test_agent_prompt_budget_gate.py` (a ceiling PLUS an exact recorded proxy-token measurement near the top of the file), and `tests/unit/test_agent_prompt_playbook_consistency_gate.py` (`test_the_real_registry_and_the_one_real_playbook_agree_on_six_tools`). All three become parametrised over every registered workflow, each with its own golden and its own ceiling. The budget gate's exact recorded measurement WILL move when shared sections are extracted — re-record it deliberately in the PR and say what it moved from and to; do not quietly loosen the ceiling instead.

There are also FOUR further prompt tests the issue does not name and that must be kept honest: `tests/unit/test_agent_prompt_optimize_product_v1_contract.py`, `..._v2_contract.py`, `..._v3_contract.py` and `tests/unit/test_agent_prompt_copy_governance_gate.py` (plus `test_agent_prompt_no_tool_fences_in_worked_example.py`). A v4 needs its own contract test alongside the v1–v3 ones; the released v1/v2/v3 files and their goldens are IMMUTABLE (ADR-072 decision 4) and must not be edited to absorb the shared sections.
NO HTTP surface, NO schema change, NO new route or response field. `workflow_runs.prompt_version`/`prompt_sha256` are existing columns; only the VALUE written into them changes.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. `prompts/` keeps one workflow's version files, `_WORKFLOW_BINDINGS` keeps its single entry, the three gate tests stay pinned to `optimize_product_2`, the production pin stays 3 and every run keeps executing exactly the v3 bytes it executes today. Nothing is exposed, nothing is partially applied, and no seller sees a change.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Code-only rollback: redeploy the previous release and restart juli-api and juli-celery-worker. There is NO schema to revert and NO downgrade to run — this slice owns no migration. The previous release restores the v3 pin for NEW runs, and v1/v2/v3 are untouched on disk and immutable (ADR-072 decision 4), so historical runs stay resolvable. THE ONE REAL HAZARD, which must be stated in the PR and asserted pre-merge: a run created on the candidate and pinned to v4, still suspended at CONFIRM when the rollback lands, will try to resume on a release whose disk has no `v4.md` — and will fail CLOSED with `prompt_version_unrecoverable` rather than silently executing v3, because consent was bound to v4's bytes. That is the correct behaviour and must be proven, not discovered. Rollback ordering therefore matters: drain or let expire the runs pinned to v4 before redeploying, or accept the named fail-closed and say so.
